A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QHNetV2 research, with matching authors, architecture and experiments. All 17 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QHNetV2 results on QH9 and MD17, together with efficiency measurements and component ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original QH9 and MD17 results and the efficiency and ablation results, with the latter studies relocated to Appendix A.

M1.justification: The specified SO(2) tensor-product computation changes from componentwise products and index flips in v1 Eqs. 5–8 to complex-product and conjugate-product formulas with cross terms and signs in v2 Eqs. 7–9. This is a localized correction to a component; the surrounding architecture and nearest-neighbor frame selection remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four QH9 settings and MD17 trajectories for water, ethanol, malondialdehyde and uracil. PubChemQH remains unevaluated future work in both versions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains QHNet across QH9, WANet on stable-id, and SPHNet on stable-id and stable-ood. Table 2 retains PhiSNet, QHNet and SPHNet for MD17, and Table 3 retains the same efficiency comparators. The new gate-comparison table is conceptual, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The splits, sample sizes, metrics, training budgets, schedules and model configurations match between v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix F. The relocated efficiency study retains the single-A6000, maximum-available-batch-size protocol.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same three SO(2) TP/FFN configurations and ablation results; the accompanying study moves from Section 5.4 to Appendix A.2. The added frame-discontinuity discussion contains no new robustness test or sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The empirical tables retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: In Table 1, QHNet's diagonal/off-diagonal MAEs on QH9-dynamic-300k-mol change from 108.70/261.63 to 261.63/108.70, in units of 10^-6 Hartree. This swaps the reported values and reverses the diagonal-error ranking against QHNetV2. The remaining benchmark, efficiency and ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained frame-averaging argument, v2 adds Appendix D derivations relating SO(2) linear operations to SO(3) tensor products and comparing gate expressivity, plus Appendix E's irrep-mapping equivariance argument. Section 3.2 also revises the tensor-product algebra. These substantially expand and revise the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: QHNetV2 uses SO(2) local-frame operations to preserve global SO(3) equivariance, avoid costly SO(3) tensor products, and perform strongly on QH9 and MD17. The symmetric-contraction analogy removed from the abstract remains in the introduction and method.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges discontinuities from nearest-neighbor frame selection and discusses averaging neighboring frames as a possible remedy. It also explicitly states that SO(2) and SO(3) tensor products are non-equivalent and that lower complexity does not guarantee better performance. Appendix D adds an expressivity explanation for SO(2) gating.

D1.justification: v1's abstract promises code release through AIRS and supplies a repository URL; v2 removes both without replacement. Software versions, hardware and appendix hyperparameters remain unchanged. This changes access information, without establishing whether code availability actually changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Pozdnyakov and Ceriotti's work on smooth rotational symmetrization and expands the discussion of continuity and relationships to eSCN. It drops v1 Section 3.1's explicit claim to be the first to connect eSCN with frame averaging. The Hamiltonian-prediction related-work survey is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 is rewritten into explicit global-frame, local-frame and irrep-mapping explanations. Hamiltonian equivariance moves from v1 Appendix A.3 into Section 2.1, while efficiency and ablation studies move into v2 Appendix A. Most existing prose remains, alongside small abstract edits and removal of acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 comparing SO(2) and SO(3) gates, relocates Tables 3–4 to the appendix, and adjusts benchmark-table sizing and emphasis. Figures 1–2 retain their drawings, with resizing or placement changes. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The corrected tensor-product formulas and Table 1 assignment improve accuracy, while the expanded frame explanation and explicit continuity/performance limitations make the method easier to assess. The empirical evidence is essentially unchanged. These gains outweigh the removed code-release information, but the new Appendix E argument contains an invalid general realignment step using a z-axis rotation, limiting the improvement in mathematical rigor.
